newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 27.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Former finance minister Tarrin Nimmanhaeminda has suggested that the government slash a further 45 billion baht from the proposed 982 billion baht budget to ensure it was a "truly balanced" one. During the second day spent debating the budget, Bangkok Democrat MP Tarrin said if the budget was not trimmed now it would have to be in the next fiscal year. (BANGKOK POST)

- The chief architect and engineer responsible for the unlawful renovation that led to the 1993 collapse of the Royal Plaza Hotel and the death of 137 people has received a 20-year prison sentence in the Nakhon Ratchasima provincial court. Five other hotel executive board members and employees are given prison terms and fined for their involvement in the disaster at the hotel, which left an additional 227 people injured - the worst building collapse the country has ever seen. (THE NATION) (BANGKOK POST)

- An ambitious Avon Products Inc hopes to use Thailand as its springboard into the emerging Indochinese markets. The chairman and chief executive officer of the company says the company is studying business potential in Laos, Cambodia and Burma and hopes to begin selling in those countries in 3-5 years. (BANGKOK POST)

- The president of Siam Cement Group has slammed the Bank of Thailand for failing to provide a sense of direction to the private sector, which is increasingly at a loss over the country's macro-economic and interest rate policies. He lashes out at the Bank of Thailand over its lack of direction in restoring economic stability and its murky measures in dealing with the troubled financial sector, a failure that has led to a deepening of the crisis of confidence. (THE NATION)
